title: Explain Elements of the Risk Management Process

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Risk management identifies uncertainty, assesses likelihood and impact, records ownership and indicators, selects a response, and communicates business consequences.
sections.callout: Identify -> assess -> analyze -> record -> respond -> report.

entries.title: Risk identification
paragraphs: Discovering threats, vulnerabilities, assets, and conditions that could affect objectives.

entries.title: Risk assessment
paragraphs: Evaluating identified risk to support prioritization and treatment.

entries.title: Ad hoc
paragraphs: Assessment performed when a particular need or event arises.

entries.title: Recurring
paragraphs: Assessment repeated on a defined schedule.

entries.title: One-time
paragraphs: Assessment performed once for a specific purpose.

entries.title: Continuous
paragraphs: Ongoing assessment using current observations and monitoring.

entries.title: Risk analysis
paragraphs: Estimating and interpreting risk using descriptive or numeric methods.

entries.title: Qualitative
paragraphs: Uses descriptive ratings such as low, medium, and high.

entries.title: Quantitative
paragraphs: Uses numbers and monetary values.

entries.title: Single loss expectancy (SLE)
paragraphs: Expected loss from one event: asset value multiplied by exposure factor.

entries.title: Annualized loss expectancy (ALE)
paragraphs: Expected yearly loss: SLE multiplied by annualized rate of occurrence.

entries.title: Annualized rate of occurrence (ARO)
paragraphs: Expected number or frequency of occurrences per year.

entries.title: Probability
paragraphs: Numeric chance that an event will occur.

entries.title: Likelihood
paragraphs: Estimated chance of an event, often expressed descriptively.

entries.title: Exposure factor
paragraphs: Percentage of asset value expected to be lost in one event.

entries.title: Impact
paragraphs: Magnitude of harm if the event occurs.

entries.title: Risk register
paragraphs: Central record of identified risks, ratings, owners, responses, and status.

entries.title: Key risk indicators
paragraphs: Metrics that signal changes in risk exposure.

entries.title: Risk owners
paragraphs: People accountable for monitoring and managing assigned risks.

entries.title: Risk threshold
paragraphs: Defined level that triggers action, escalation, or review.

entries.title: Risk tolerance
paragraphs: Acceptable variation around objectives or acceptable risk range.

entries.title: Risk appetite
paragraphs: Amount and type of risk the organization is willing to pursue or retain.

entries.title: Expansionary
paragraphs: Higher willingness to accept risk in pursuit of growth or opportunity.

entries.title: Conservative
paragraphs: Lower willingness to accept risk; protection and stability are emphasized.

entries.title: Neutral
paragraphs: Balanced willingness to accept risk.

entries.title: Risk management strategies
paragraphs: Available approaches for treating risk.

entries.title: Transfer
paragraphs: Shift specified financial consequences to another party, such as through insurance or contract.

entries.title: Accept
paragraphs: Knowingly retain risk without additional mitigation.

entries.title: Exemption
paragraphs: Formal release from a requirement for a defined scope.

entries.title: Exception
paragraphs: Approved, commonly temporary, deviation from a requirement.

entries.title: Avoid
paragraphs: Stop the activity that creates the risk.

entries.title: Mitigate
paragraphs: Reduce likelihood or impact through controls.

entries.title: Risk reporting
paragraphs: Communicating risk status, trends, ownership, and decisions to stakeholders.

entries.title: Business impact analysis
paragraphs: Determines how disruption affects critical business functions, dependencies, and recovery priorities.

entries.title: Recovery time objective (RTO)
paragraphs: Maximum targeted time to restore a service.
entries.recognitionCue: How long can restoration take? -> RTO

entries.title: Recovery point objective (RPO)
paragraphs: Maximum acceptable data-loss interval measured in time.
entries.recognitionCue: How much recent data can be lost? -> RPO

entries.title: Mean time to repair (MTTR)
paragraphs: Average time required to restore a failed component.

entries.title: Mean time between failures (MTBF)
paragraphs: Average operating time expected between failures.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Descriptive rating = qualitative; numeric or monetary estimate = quantitative
SLE = asset value x exposure factor; ALE = SLE x ARO
Risk appetite is broad willingness; tolerance is acceptable variation; threshold triggers action
RTO measures restoration time; RPO measures acceptable data-loss time
MTTR measures repair speed; MTBF measures reliability between failures

sections.title: Objective 5.2 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Transfer does not eliminate risk; it shifts specified consequences. An exception is an approved deviation, while an exemption releases a defined scope from a requirement. RTO concerns downtime, while RPO concerns recoverable data age.
sections.callout: Determine whether the clue concerns assessment timing, analysis method, governance boundary, treatment choice, or recovery metric.

miniCheck.intro: Choose the correct risk metric for each clue.
miniCheck.prompt: A business can tolerate no more than four hours before a critical service is restored, and it can accept losing no more than fifteen minutes of recently created data.

fields.label: Metric defining the four-hour restoration target
Metric defining the fifteen-minute data-loss limit

miniCheck.correctFeedback: Correct. RTO sets the restoration-time target, while RPO sets the maximum acceptable data-loss interval.
miniCheck.retryFeedback: Not quite. Separate how long service restoration may take from how much recent data may be lost.
